1 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Sathankulam, dated 09.07.2009 in C.C.No.105 of 2.The

respondent police has filed charge sheet against the revision petitioner herein for the offences punishable under Sections 7(i) and 16(i)(a)(i) and (ii) r/w 2 (ia) (a) and (m) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 before the learned Judicial Magistrate, Sathankulam.

3.Before the trial Court to substantiate the charges, the prosecution has examined P.W.1 and P.W.2 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.20.
4.On consideration of both oral and documentary evidence adduced before the trial Court, the learned Judicial Magistrate, Sathankulam has convicted the accused and sentenced to undergo http://www.judis.nic.in simple imprisonment for three months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/- in default to undergo simple imprisonment for two months for the offenses as stated supra.

5.On appeal in Crl.A.No.72 of 2009, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, has dismissed the same,
confirming the judgment of the trial Court.
Aggrieved against the same, the petitioner / accused has approached this Court by way of filing this Criminal Revision Case.

6.The learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that both the Courts below have miserably failed to see that there is a considerable delay in lodging the prosecution for the alleged adulteration of Maida, which said to have been contained 0.33% Alcoholic Acidity as against permitted limitation of 0.12% as per Ex.P.13, report of the Lab, which is said to have been received on 19.04.2004 in Form 13.

However, the complaint for prosecution has been lodged before the competent Jurisdictional Court on 10.07.2006 with delay of almost two years and copy of Ex.P.13,
lab test has been served upon the accused on 12.08.2006, which according to the revision petitioner is violation of the mandatory statutory period, http://www.judis.nic.in namely, beyond period of 10 days as prescribed in Rule 9(B) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

7.He also relied upon the following decisions in the case of:-
(i) State by Food Inspector, Cumbam... Vs. Jafar Ali on 06.02.2004.
(ii) State by Food Inspector, Trichy Vs. Paulraj, on 11.02.2004.

(vi) Murugesan and another Vs. State represented by the Food Inspector, Cumbum Municipality,
Cumbum, Theni District on 24.11.2017.
8.The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) appearing for the respondent has made submissions in support of the judgment of the trial Court.

9.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) appearing for the respondent and perused the materials available on record carefully.
10.Point for consideration in this Criminal Revision Case is that whether the right of the accused in sending the sample taken by the prosecution to Central Food Laboratory at the instance of the accused has been vitiated or withheld due to deliberate delay in lodging the prosecution or not?.

11.It is seen from the records that the samples Ex.P.5 were taken on 13.03.2004 and public analyst report Ex.P.12 was received by the complainant on 30.04.2004 and the prosecution was instituted http://www.judis.nic.in on 04.08.2006 and the case was taken on file on 09.08.2006 and statutory notice under Section 13(2) (Ex.P.17) was served on the petitioner on 12.08.2006 i.e., after 28 months from 13.03.2004 when the samples were taken.
Therefore, the petitioner was denied his right as envisaged under Section 13(3) of the Act on account of the deliberate conduct of the prosecution.
As a result of which, the sample got highly decomposed and could not be analysed and thereby the petitioner was seriously prejudiced.
Since the sample of the food article was deteriorated and decomposed, no analysis is possible and thereby the right of the petitioner is frustrated.

Therefore, the conviction and sentence passed by the Courts below cannot be sustained.
12.After going through the dates and events as mentioned above, I am of the considered view that the ratio laid down in the judgement as stated supra, is squarely applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case and hence, the conviction and sentence passed by the Courts below is not sustainable in law.
In this view of the matter, the conviction and sentence passed by the Courts below is hereby set aside.
http://www.judis.nic.in
13.In the result
, this Criminal Revision Case is allowed.
The revision petitioner / accused is acquitted.
Fine amount, if any, paid by the petitioner shall be refunded to him.
Bail bond executed by the petitioner and the sureties shall stand terminated.
